301	        self, global_steps: int, partition_id: str
302	    ) -> tuple[set[str], set[str], set[str], Counter]:
303	        """Return stale, DAPO-filtered, and failed groups (plus the DAPO value->count breakdown).
304	
305	        The three sets may overlap. Callers clear and refill their union, so one prompt is never handled
306	        twice. ``dapo_counts`` is the {shared_metric_value: group_count} diagnostic for ``dapo_uids``; it
307	        rides along in the return value so no hidden state is needed between production and consumption.
308	        """
309	        if partition_id == "val":
310	            return set(), set(), set(), Counter()
311	
312	        dapo_uids, dapo_counts = self._dapo_filtered_keys(partition_id)
313	        failed_uids = set()
314	        if self.sync_refill_failed_groups:
315	            materializable_uids = {key.split("_")[0] for key in self.partitions[partition_id]}
316	            failed_uids = self.failure_keys[partition_id] - materializable_uids
317	        return set(), dapo_uids, failed_uids, dapo_counts

319	    def _sampleable_terminal_keys(
320	        self,
321	        partition_id: str,
322	        eviction_reasons: tuple[set[str], set[str], set[str], Counter],
323	    ) -> set[str]:
324	        terminal_uids = self.finished_keys[partition_id] | self.failure_keys[partition_id]
325	        stale_uids, dapo_uids, failed_uids, _dapo_counts = eviction_reasons
326	        return terminal_uids - (stale_uids | dapo_uids | failed_uids)

328	    def _evict_terminal_groups(
329	        self,
330	        global_steps: int,
331	        partition_id: str,
332	        eviction_reasons: tuple[set[str], set[str], set[str], Counter],
333	    ) -> tuple[set[str], int, int, dict]:
334	        """Evict terminal groups selected by any active policy exactly once."""
335	        stale_uids, dapo_uids, failed_uids, dapo_counts = eviction_reasons
336	        evicted_uids = stale_uids | dapo_uids | failed_uids
337	        if not evicted_uids:
338	            return set(), 0, 0, {}
339	
340	        prefix = self._metrics_prefix(partition_id)
341	        metrics: dict = {}
342	        if stale_uids:
343	            prompt_global_steps = self.prompt_global_steps[partition_id]
344	            spans = np.array(
345	                [global_steps - prompt_global_steps.get(uid, global_steps) + 1 for uid in stale_uids],
346	                dtype=float,
347	            )
348	            metrics.update(
349	                {
350	                    f"{prefix}/off_policy/evicted_samples": len(stale_uids),
351	                    f"{prefix}/off_policy/evicted_samples_staleness/mean": spans.mean(),
352	                    f"{prefix}/off_policy/evicted_samples_staleness/max": spans.max(),
353	                    f"{prefix}/off_policy/evicted_samples_staleness/min": spans.min(),
354	                }
355	            )
356	        if dapo_uids:
357	            metrics[f"{prefix}/filter_groups/evicted_samples"] = len(dapo_uids)
358	            # Non-scalar diagnostic: how many filtered (no-signal) groups collapsed to each metric value.
359	            metrics[DAPO_FILTERED_REWARD_COUNTS_KEY] = dict(dapo_counts)
360	        if failed_uids:
361	            metrics[f"{prefix}/rollout_failure/evicted_samples"] = len(failed_uids)
362	
363	        self._clear_groups(partition_id, evicted_uids)
364	        return evicted_uids, len(stale_uids), len(dapo_uids), metrics

406	        """Sample a batch using synchronous rollout semantics.
407	
408	        NOTE: user can customize sampling strategy by setting:
409	        ```bash
410	        trainer.v1.sampler.custom_sampler.path = "path/to/your/sampler.py"
411	        trainer.v1.sampler.custom_sampler.name = "UserCustomReplayBuffer"
412	        ```
413	
414	        Args:
415	            global_steps (int): Global steps of the current training.
416	            partition_id (str): Partition of TransferQueue, e.g. "train" or "val".
417	            batch_size (int, optional): Batch size.
418	
419	        Returns:
420	            KVBatchMeta: A batch of data.
421	            dict: Auxiliary metrics.
422	        """
423	        last_debug_time = time.time()
424	        eviction_metrics: dict = {}
425	        dapo_enabled = partition_id != "val" and self.filter_groups_metric is not None
426	        refill_credit = 0
427	        draining = False
428	        max_inflight_prompts = 0
429	        if dapo_enabled:
430	            max_inflight_prompts = self.max_inflight_gen_batches * self.train_batch_size
431	
432	        while True:
433	            # Eviction, gating, and selection below must all use this snapshot.
434	            self._sync_metadata_from_transfer_queue()

860	def calc_maj_val(data: list[dict[str, Any]], vote_key: str, val_key: str) -> float:
861	    """
862	    Calculate a value based on majority voting.
863	
864	    This function identifies the most common value for a specified vote key
865	    in the data, then returns the corresponding value for that majority vote.
866	
867	    Args:
868	        data: List of dictionaries, where each dictionary contains both vote_key and val_key.
869	        vote_key: The key in each dictionary used for voting/counting.
870	        val_key: The key in each dictionary whose value will be returned for the majority vote.
871	
872	    Returns:
873	        The value associated with the most common vote.
874	
875	    Example:
876	        >>> data = [
877	        ...     {"pred": "A", "val": 0.9},
878	        ...     {"pred": "B", "val": 0.8},
879	        ...     {"pred": "A", "val": 0.7}
880	        ... ]
881	        >>> calc_maj_val(data, vote_key="pred", val_key="val")
882	        0.9  # Returns the first "val" for the majority vote "A"
883	    """
884	    vote2vals = defaultdict(list)
885	    for d in data:
886	        vote2vals[d[vote_key]].append(d[val_key])
887	
888	    vote2cnt = {k: len(v) for k, v in vote2vals.items()}
889	    maj_vote = max(vote2cnt, key=vote2cnt.get)
890	
891	    maj_val = vote2vals[maj_vote][0]
892	
893	    return maj_val

import logging

import torch

from verl.protocol import DataProto

logger = logging.getLogger(__file__)


def calculate_token_list_diff(tensor1: torch.Tensor, tensor2: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    # verify inputs
    if tensor1.numel() == 0 or tensor2.numel() == 0:
        return torch.zeros(tensor1.shape[0], dtype=torch.long, device=tensor1.device)
    if tensor1.shape != tensor2.shape or mask.shape != tensor1.shape or mask.shape != tensor2.shape:
        print(
            f"<WARN> dim of tensor1, tensor2, mask is not equal, {(tensor1.shape)=},{(tensor2.shape)=}, {(mask.shape)=}"
        )
        return torch.ones_like(tensor1)
    # transfer to same device
    if tensor2.device != tensor1.device:
        tensor2 = tensor2.to(tensor1.device)
    if mask.device != tensor1.device:
        mask = mask.to(tensor1.device)

    # calculate diff
    diff_mask = tensor1 != tensor2

    valid_diff_mask = diff_mask & (mask == 1)

    diff_counts = valid_diff_mask.sum(dim=1)

    return diff_counts


def pearson_correlation_coefficient(tensor1: torch.Tensor, tensor2: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    # implemention of https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13585
    if tensor1.shape != tensor2.shape or mask.shape != tensor1.shape or mask.shape != tensor2.shape:
        return 0
    mt1 = torch.masked_select(tensor1, mask)
    mt2 = torch.masked_select(tensor2, mask)
    result = torch.corrcoef(torch.stack([mt1, mt2], dim=0))
    return result[0][1].detach().item()


def calculate_log_prob_diff(log_probs1: torch.Tensor, log_probs2: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    full_diff = torch.abs(log_probs1 - log_probs2)
    return torch.masked_select(full_diff, mask)


def calculate_debug_metrics(data: DataProto) -> dict:
    """
    calculate rollout vs actor logprobs diff, for debugging purpose

    Args:
        data: DataProto
            the data batch to calculate
            rollout_log_probs: log_probs record when rollout forward tokens
            old_log_probs(actor log probs): log_probs record when actor forward tokens
            loss_mask or attention_mask: to mask unrelated token
            responses: the response tokens, for calculating size
    Returns:
        dict: metrics
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 1->input is valid, 0->input is invalid
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": max value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": mean value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": std value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
            "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": logprob's pearson corrcoef of rollout vs. actor, reference to https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13585
    """

    rollout_old_log_probs = data.batch["rollout_log_probs"]
    actor_old_log_probs = data.batch["old_log_probs"]
    if "response_mask" in data.batch:
        logger.debug("response mask found, use it to mask log probs")
        log_prob_mask = data.batch["response_mask"]
    elif "attention_mask" in data.batch:
        log_prob_mask = data.batch["attention_mask"]
    else:
        logger.warning(f"no mask info found, use all log probs, {(data.batch.keys())=}")
        log_prob_mask = torch.ones_like(rollout_old_log_probs)
    responses = data.batch["responses"]
    response_length = responses.size(1)

    response_mask = log_prob_mask[:, -response_length:]
    # calculate pearson corrcoef
    actor_probs = torch.exp(actor_old_log_probs)
    rollout_probs = torch.exp(rollout_old_log_probs)
    response_mask_bool = response_mask.bool()

    # check if there are any valid tokens before computing metrics
    if not response_mask_bool.any():
        logger.warning("response_mask is all False, returning default metrics")
        return {
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 0,
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": float("nan"),
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": float("nan"),
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": float("nan"),
            "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": float("nan"),
        }

    pearson_corrcoef = pearson_correlation_coefficient(actor_probs, rollout_probs, response_mask_bool)
    rollout_probs_diff = calculate_log_prob_diff(actor_probs, rollout_probs, response_mask_bool)
    return {
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 1,
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": torch.max(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": torch.mean(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": torch.std(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
        "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": pearson_corrcoef,
    }

50	    if tensor1.shape != tensor2.shape or mask.shape != tensor1.shape or mask.shape != tensor2.shape:
51	        return 0
52	    mt1 = torch.masked_select(tensor1, mask)
53	    mt2 = torch.masked_select(tensor2, mask)
54	    result = torch.corrcoef(torch.stack([mt1, mt2], dim=0))
55	    return result[0][1].detach().item()

58	def calculate_log_prob_diff(log_probs1: torch.Tensor, log_probs2: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
59	    full_diff = torch.abs(log_probs1 - log_probs2)
60	    return torch.masked_select(full_diff, mask)

63	def calculate_debug_metrics(data: DataProto) -> dict:
64	    """
65	    calculate rollout vs actor logprobs diff, for debugging purpose
66	
67	    Args:
68	        data: DataProto
69	            the data batch to calculate
70	            rollout_log_probs: log_probs record when rollout forward tokens
71	            old_log_probs(actor log probs): log_probs record when actor forward tokens
72	            loss_mask or attention_mask: to mask unrelated token
73	            responses: the response tokens, for calculating size
74	    Returns:
75	        dict: metrics
76	            "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 1->input is valid, 0->input is invalid
77	            "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": max value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
78	            "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": mean value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
79	            "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": std value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
80	            "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": logprob's pearson corrcoef of rollout vs. actor, reference to https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13585
81	    """
82	
83	    rollout_old_log_probs = data.batch["rollout_log_probs"]
84	    actor_old_log_probs = data.batch["old_log_probs"]
85	    if "response_mask" in data.batch:
86	        logger.debug("response mask found, use it to mask log probs")
87	        log_prob_mask = data.batch["response_mask"]
88	    elif "attention_mask" in data.batch:
89	        log_prob_mask = data.batch["attention_mask"]
90	    else:
91	        logger.warning(f"no mask info found, use all log probs, {(data.batch.keys())=}")
92	        log_prob_mask = torch.ones_like(rollout_old_log_probs)
93	    responses = data.batch["responses"]
94	    response_length = responses.size(1)
95	
96	    response_mask = log_prob_mask[:, -response_length:]
97	    # calculate pearson corrcoef
98	    actor_probs = torch.exp(actor_old_log_probs)
99	    rollout_probs = torch.exp(rollout_old_log_probs)
100	    response_mask_bool = response_mask.bool()
101	
102	    # check if there are any valid tokens before computing metrics
103	    if not response_mask_bool.any():
104	        logger.warning("response_mask is all False, returning default metrics")
105	        return {
106	            "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 0,
107	            "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": float("nan"),
108	            "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": float("nan"),
109	            "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": float("nan"),
110	            "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": float("nan"),
111	        }
112	
113	    pearson_corrcoef = pearson_correlation_coefficient(actor_probs, rollout_probs, response_mask_bool)
114	    rollout_probs_diff = calculate_log_prob_diff(actor_probs, rollout_probs, response_mask_bool)
115	    return {
116	        "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 1,
117	        "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": torch.max(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
118	        "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": torch.mean(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
119	        "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": torch.std(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
120	        "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": pearson_corrcoef,
121	    }

647	    def _get_packed_pad_size(self, packed_length: int) -> int:
648	        """Right-padding that rounds a packed micro-batch up to the next bucket boundary.
649	
650	        ``rearrange_micro_batches`` derives the *number* of micro-batches from the token budget but
651	        chooses their *contents* to balance attention workload (Σ seqlen²), so a micro-batch's token
652	        count is neither constant nor bounded by that budget. Bucketing therefore beats padding to
653	        the budget itself, which would leave every over-budget micro-batch fully dynamic while
654	        making every under-budget one pay a full-budget forward.
655	        """
656	        if not self.pad_to_length:
657	            return 0
658	        bucket = self.pad_to_length_bucket
659	        return ceildiv(packed_length, bucket) * bucket - packed_length
660	
661	    def _gather_and_unpad_packed(self, tensor: torch.Tensor, pad_size: int) -> torch.Tensor:
662	        """Strip what ``prepare_model_inputs`` appended to the packed sequence.
663	
664	        Under Ulysses SP the per-rank shards are all-gathered back into the global packed
665	        sequence first. ``pad_size`` covers both the SP-alignment pad and the static pad from
666	        :meth:`_get_packed_pad_size`; both sit at the tail of the global sequence.
667	        """
668	        if self.use_ulysses_sp:
669	            return gather_outputs_and_unpad(tensor, gather_dim=0, unpad_dim=0, padding_size=pad_size)
670	        return tensor[:-pad_size] if pad_size else tensor

672	    @contextmanager
673	    def _gradient_sync_context(self, *, is_last_micro_batch: bool):
674	        """Skip FSDP gradient communication on non-final accumulation steps.
675	
676	        During gradient accumulation the optimizer only steps after the final
677	        micro-batch, so gradients only need to be synchronized once per
678	        mini-batch. Deferring synchronization on the non-final micro-batches
679	        reduces FSDP gradient collectives from one reduce-scatter per
680	        micro-batch to a single round, at the cost of temporarily retaining
681	        unsharded gradients until the final backward.
682	        """
683	        if is_last_micro_batch:
684	            yield
685	            return
686	
687	        version = fsdp_version(self.module)
688	        if version == 1:
689	            with self.module.no_sync():
690	                yield
691	        elif version == 2:
692	            self.module.set_requires_gradient_sync(False)
693	            try:
694	                yield
695	            finally:
696	                self.module.set_requires_gradient_sync(True)
697	        else:
698	            yield

700	    def forward_backward_batch(self, data: TensorDict, loss_function: Callable, forward_only=False) -> list[TensorDict]:
701	        # note that the global_batch_size should include data on all the dp
702	        tu.assign_non_tensor(data, sp_size=self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size)
703	        return_model_output = tu.get_non_tensor_data(data=data, key="return_model_output", default=False)
704	
705	        # compute num_tokens in global batch for loss normalization
706	        batch_num_tokens = data["loss_mask"].sum().to(get_device_id())
707	        torch.distributed.all_reduce(
708	            batch_num_tokens, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.SUM, group=self.get_data_parallel_group()
709	        )
710	        tu.assign_non_tensor(data, batch_num_tokens=batch_num_tokens.item())
711	        tu.assign_non_tensor(data, dp_size=self.get_data_parallel_size())
712	
713	        micro_batches, indices = prepare_micro_batches(
714	            data=data, dp_group=self.get_data_parallel_group(), same_micro_num_in_dp=True
715	        )
716	
717	        output_lst = []
718	
719	        ctx = torch.no_grad() if forward_only else nullcontext()
720	
721	        # getattr fallback: some subclasses (e.g. VeOmniEngine) bypass FSDPEngine.__init__
722	        # and _build_fsdp_module, so self.scaler may not be set.
723	        scaler = getattr(self, "scaler", None)
724	
725	        for micro_batch_idx, micro_batch in enumerate(micro_batches):
726	            sync_ctx = (
727	                nullcontext()
728	                if forward_only
729	                else self._gradient_sync_context(is_last_micro_batch=micro_batch_idx == len(micro_batches) - 1)
730	            )
731	            with ctx, sync_ctx:
732	                loss, meta_info = self.forward_step(micro_batch, loss_function=loss_function, forward_only=forward_only)
733	
734	                if not forward_only:
735	                    if scaler is not None:
736	                        scaler.scale(loss).backward()
737	                    else:
738	                        loss.backward()
739	                    if not return_model_output:
740	                        # Standard training discards model_output (train_batch pops it); keeping it accumulates
741	                        # full-length nested tensors across the mini-batch (∝ ppo_mini_batch * rollout_n) → OOM.
742	                        # Specialized callers such as Tinker may opt in when their response requires these outputs.
743	                        meta_info.pop("model_output", None)
744	
745	            output_lst.append(meta_info)
746	
747	        # postprocess and return
748	        return postprocess_batch_func(output_lst=output_lst, indices=indices, data=data)

759	    def optimizer_step(self):
760	        """
761	        Clip gradients, skip update if non-finite, and step optimizer.
762	
763	        Returns:
764	            grad_norm (float): Norm of gradients before clipping.
765	        """
766	        assert self.optimizer_config.clip_grad is not None
767	
768	        # getattr fallback: some subclasses (e.g. VeOmniEngine) bypass FSDPEngine.__init__.
769	        scaler = getattr(self, "scaler", None)
770	
771	        # Unscale gradients before clip so the clip threshold is applied to true gradient
772	        # magnitudes, not scaled ones. scaler.step() will skip the update if any grad is inf/nan.
773	        if scaler is not None:
774	            scaler.unscale_(self.optimizer)
775	
776	        if isinstance(self.module, FSDP):
777	            grad_norm = self.module.clip_grad_norm_(self.optimizer_config.clip_grad)
778	        elif isinstance(self.module, FSDPModule):
779	            grad_norm = fsdp2_clip_grad_norm_(self.module.parameters(), max_norm=self.optimizer_config.clip_grad)
780	        else:
781	            grad_norm = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(
782	                self.module.parameters(), max_norm=self.optimizer_config.clip_grad
783	            )
784	
785	        if isinstance(grad_norm, DTensor):
786	            grad_norm = grad_norm.full_tensor()
787	
788	        if scaler is not None:
789	            # scaler handles inf/nan skipping internally via _check_inf_per_device.
790	            scaler.step(self.optimizer)
791	            scaler.update()
792	        else:
793	            # if grad_norm is not finite, skip the update
794	            if not torch.isfinite(grad_norm):
795	                print(f"WARN: grad_norm is not finite: {grad_norm}")
796	                self.optimizer.zero_grad()
797	            else:
798	                self.optimizer.step()
799	
800	        if self._qat_enabled:
801	            from verl.utils.qat.core import invalidate_all_scales
802	
803	            invalidate_all_scales(self.module)
804	
805	        return grad_norm.item()

890	    def get_per_tensor_param_shard(self, **kwargs):
891	        """Like :meth:`get_per_tensor_param`, but yields each rank's *local* FSDP shard
892	        ``(name, local_flat_shard_bf16, ShardSpec)`` instead of all-gathering the full
893	        tensor. Pure DTensor export, no side effects -- delta bookkeeping lives in
894	        :meth:`get_per_tensor_param_delta_shard`. Non-LoRA base path only."""
895	
896	        # FSDP1's (SHARDED_)STATE_DICT export runs through the unshard machinery and
897	        # asserts flat params are GPU-resident; FSDP2 state_dict() only collects
898	        # DTensor refs and the generator below stages each shard lazily.
899	        _needs_staging = fsdp_version(self.module) == 1
900	        if _needs_staging and not self._uses_fsdp2_cpu_offload_policy:
901	            load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.module)
902	        params = self.module.state_dict()
903	        params = convert_weight_keys(params, getattr(self.module, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.module))
904	        if _needs_staging and self._is_offload_param:
905	            offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu(self.module)
906	
907	        device = get_device_id()
908	
909	        from ..spec import ShardSpec
910	
911	        def _gen():
912	            for name, param in params.items():
913	                spec = ShardSpec.from_param(param)
914	                p = param.to(device, non_blocking=True)
915	                if p.is_floating_point():
916	                    p = p.to(torch.bfloat16, non_blocking=True)
917	                local = p.to_local() if hasattr(p, "to_local") else p
918	                yield name, local.reshape(-1), spec

1035	    def _merged_lora_per_tensor_param(self):
1036	        """Stream merged (base + LoRA) weights for rollout weight sync.
1037	
1038	        ``state_dict()`` returns tensors that alias the live FSDP parameter
1039	        storage, and ``merged_lora_context`` restores the un-merged base
1040	        weights when it exits. The context therefore must stay open until the
1041	        consumer has materialized every tensor: ``DTensor.full_tensor()``
1042	        produces a copy, so yielded tensors remain valid after the restore.
1043	        Consuming a state_dict captured inside the context after the context
1044	        has exited would silently send base weights without the adapters.
1045	        """
1046	        device = get_device_id()
1047	        try:
1048	            with merged_lora_context(self.module, backup_adapters=True):
1049	                params = normalize_peft_param_name(self.module.state_dict())
1050	                params = convert_weight_keys(params, getattr(self.module, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.module))
1051	                for name, param in params.items():
1052	                    yield (
1053	                        name,
1054	                        param.to(device, non_blocking=True).full_tensor().to(torch.bfloat16, non_blocking=True)
1055	                        if isinstance(param, DTensor)
1056	                        # clone: plain tensors also alias module storage, and bucketed
1057	                        # senders may flush after the restore has already run
1058	                        else param.detach().clone(),
1059	                    )
1060	        finally:
1061	            log_gpu_memory_usage("Before offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu", logger=logger)
1062	            if self._is_offload_param:
1063	                offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu(self.module)
1064	            log_gpu_memory_usage("After offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu", logger=logger)
1065

1067	        return self.module.disable_adapter()

1518	        autocast_ctx: ContextManager = (
1519	            nullcontext()
1520	            if autocast_dtype == torch.float32
1521	            else torch.autocast(device_type=device_name, dtype=autocast_dtype)
1522	        )

1526	                use_cache=False,

1533	            if loss_function is not None:
1534	                loss, metrics = loss_function(

1536	                )
1537	            else:

1549	            model_output = {

1374	    def _compute_reward_colocate(self, batch: KVBatchMeta, metrics: dict | None = None) -> KVBatchMeta:
1375	        """Compute the reward score with a colocated reward model."""
1376	        assert self.reward_loop_manager is not None, "RewardLoopManager is None"
1377	
1378	        # 1. read the fields required by the reward model from TransferQueue.
1379	        fields = ["prompts", "responses", "raw_prompt"]
1380	        data = tq.kv_batch_get(keys=batch.keys, partition_id=batch.partition_id, select_fields=fields)
1381	
1382	        prompt_lengths = data["prompts"].offsets().diff()
1383	        response_lengths = data["responses"].offsets().diff()
1384	        prompts = data["prompts"].to_padded_tensor(padding=self.tokenizer.pad_token_id)
1385	        responses = data["responses"].to_padded_tensor(padding=self.tokenizer.pad_token_id)
1386	
1387	        # 2. rebuild the attention mask aligned with the [prompts | responses] layout.
1388	        prompt_mask = self._lengths_to_mask(prompt_lengths, prompts.size(1))
1389	        response_mask = self._lengths_to_mask(response_lengths, responses.size(1))
1390	        attention_mask = torch.cat([prompt_mask, response_mask], dim=1)
1391	
1392	        # `raw_prompt` is a non-tensor field; depending on the TransferQueue backend it
1393	        # comes back as a tensordict LinkedList (a `list` subclass), a NonTensorStack or a
1394	        # numpy array. `list(...)` normalizes all of them to a plain list where each element
1395	        # is one sample's chat-message list (whereas `.tolist()` only exists on numpy/tensors).
1396	        raw_prompts = list(data["raw_prompt"])
1397	        raw_prompt_arr = np.empty(len(raw_prompts), dtype=object)
1398	        raw_prompt_arr[:] = raw_prompts
1399	
1400	        rm_input = DataProto(
1401	            batch=TensorDict(
1402	                {"prompts": prompts, "responses": responses, "attention_mask": attention_mask},
1403	                batch_size=len(batch),
1404	            ),
1405	            non_tensor_batch={"raw_prompt": raw_prompt_arr},
1406	        )
1407	
1408	        # 3. run the reward model (wakes/sleeps the reward model internally).
1409	        rm_output = self.reward_loop_manager.compute_rm_score(rm_input)
1410	
1411	        # 4. write rm_scores (and reward extra info) back to TransferQueue.
1412	        padded_rm_scores = rm_output.batch["rm_scores"]
1413	        rm_scores = torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(
1414	            [padded_rm_scores[i, : response_lengths[i]] for i in range(len(batch))],
1415	            layout=torch.jagged,
1416	        )
1417	        write_back = {"rm_scores": rm_scores}
1418	        for key in rm_output.meta_info.get("reward_extra_keys", []):

1420	        tq.kv_batch_put(
1421	            keys=batch.keys,

29	def _score_timeout(seconds: Optional[float]):
30	    """Raise ``TimeoutError`` if the wrapped block runs longer than ``seconds``.
31	
32	    A single ``compute_score`` call on a pathological model output (e.g. a long,
33	    degenerate RL rollout that triggers catastrophic regex backtracking or a slow
34	    symbolic comparison) can run for a very long time. Because ``NaiveRewardManager``
35	    scores samples serially in the driver process, one such call blocks the entire
36	    training loop. This guard bounds the wall-clock time of each call.
37	
38	    Implemented with ``SIGALRM``, so it only takes effect on the main thread. If a
39	    handler cannot be installed (e.g. called from a non-main thread), it degrades to
40	    a no-op so reward computation still runs -- just without the timeout.
41	    """
42	    if not seconds or seconds <= 0:
43	        yield
44	        return
45	
46	    def _handler(signum, frame):
47	        raise TimeoutError(f"compute_score timed out after {seconds}s")
48	
49	    try:
50	        old_handler = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _handler)
51	    except ValueError:
52	        # Not in the main thread -> SIGALRM is unavailable; run without a timeout.
53	        yield
54	        return
55	
56	    signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, seconds)
57	    try:
58	        yield
59	    finally:
60	        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
61	        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old_handler)

39	def migrate_legacy_reward_impl(config):
40	    """
41	    Migrate the legacy reward model implementation to the new one.
42	    """
43	    # 1. reward workers migration
44	    # config.reward_model.num_workers -> config.reward.num_workers
45	    if config.reward_model.num_workers is not None:
46	        config.reward.num_workers = config.reward_model.num_workers
47	
48	    # 2. reward manager migration
49	    # config.reward_model.reward_manager -> config.reward.reward_manager
50	    if config.reward_model.reward_manager is not None:
51	        config.reward.reward_manager.name = config.reward_model.reward_manager
52	    if config.reward_model.reward_loop_source is not None:
53	        config.reward.reward_manager.source = config.reward_model.reward_loop_source
54	        config.reward.reward_manager.module.path = config.reward_model.reward_loop_module_path
55	        config.reward.reward_manager.module.name = config.reward_model.reward_loop_class_name
56	
57	    # 3. custom reward function migration
58	    # config.custom_reward_function -> config.reward.custom_reward_function
59	    if not all(v is None for v in config.custom_reward_function.values()):
60	        config.reward.custom_reward_function = config.custom_reward_function
61	
62	    # 4. reward model migration
63	    # config.reward_model -> config.reward.reward_model
64	    for key in ["enable", "enable_resource_pool", "n_gpus_per_node", "nnodes"]:
65	        if config.reward_model.get(key) is not None:
66	            config.reward.reward_model[key] = config.reward_model[key]
67	    if config.reward_model.model.path is not None:
68	        config.reward.reward_model.model_path = config.reward_model.model.path
69	    # config.reward_model.reward_kwargs -> config.reward.reward_kwargs (for dapo algo)
70	    if config.reward_model.get("reward_kwargs") is not None:
71	        with open_dict(config.reward):
72	            config.reward["reward_kwargs"] = config.reward_model["reward_kwargs"]
73	    # config.reward_model.rollout -> config.reward.reward_model.rollout
74	    legacy_rollout = config.reward_model.rollout
75	    for key in legacy_rollout.keys():
76	        if legacy_rollout[key] is not None:
77	            config.reward.reward_model.rollout[key] = legacy_rollout[key]
78	
79	    # 5. sandbox_fusion migration
80	    # config.sandbox_fusion -> reward.sandbox_fusion
81	    if not all(v is None for v in config.sandbox_fusion.values()):
82	        config.reward.sandbox_fusion = config.sandbox_fusion
83	
84	    # 6. delete legacy config from configs
85	    with open_dict(config):
86	        del config.reward_model
87	        del config.custom_reward_function
88	        del config.sandbox_fusion
89	
90	    return config

93	class RewardLoopWorker:
94	    """
95	    RewardLoopWork can tackle reward computation:
96	    (1) rule-based reward computation
97	    (2) reward model-based reward computation (both disrm and genrm)
98	    (3) high-flexible user-customized reward function (can access rm by posting requests to reward_model_router)
99	
100	    Reward Computation Logic:
101	    - if user-customized reward function is provided:
102	        -> directly use user-customized reward function
103	    - if user-customized reward function is not provided:
104	        -> rm is not enabled: use default rule-based reward function
105	        -> rm is disrm: compute reward score using disrm
106	        -> rm is genrm: raise error (user-costomized reward func must be provided)
107	    """
108	
109	    def __init__(self, config: DictConfig, reward_router_address: str = None):
110	        """
111	        Args:
112	            config: DictConfig, the config for reward loop worker.
113	            reward_router_address: str, the address of reward router.
114	        """
115	        self.config = config
116	        self.reward_router_address = reward_router_address
117	        self._init_reward_fn()
118	        self.loop = get_event_loop()
119	
120	    def _init_reward_fn(self):
121	        input_tokenizer_path = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.model.tokenizer_path
122	        if input_tokenizer_path is None:
123	            input_tokenizer_path = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.model.path
124	        input_tokenizer_local_path = copy_to_local(input_tokenizer_path)
125	        self.input_tokenizer = hf_tokenizer(input_tokenizer_local_path, trust_remote_code=True)
126	        self.reward_model_tokenizer = None
127	        if self.config.reward.reward_model.enable:
128	            reward_model_tokenizer_local_path = copy_to_local(self.config.reward.reward_model.model_path)
129	            self.reward_model_tokenizer = hf_tokenizer(reward_model_tokenizer_local_path, trust_remote_code=True)
130	
131	        self.reward_manager = load_reward_manager(
132	            self.config,
133	            self.input_tokenizer,
134	            reward_router_address=self.reward_router_address,
135	            reward_model_tokenizer=self.reward_model_tokenizer,
136	        )
137	
138	    async def compute_score_batch(self, data: DataProto) -> list[dict]:
139	        tasks = []
140	        for i in range(len(data)):
141	            tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self.compute_score(data[i : i + 1])))
142	        outputs = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
143	        return outputs
144	
145	    async def compute_score(self, data: DataProto) -> dict:
146	        if self.config.reward.custom_reward_function.path is not None:
147	            # directly use user-customized reward function
148	            return await self.reward_manager.run_single(data)
149	        else:
150	            if self.config.reward.reward_model.enable:
151	                # we assume the rm is disrm
152	                # genrm must set custom_reward_function
153	                return await self.compute_score_disrm(data[-1:])
154	            else:
155	                return await self.reward_manager.run_single(data)
156	
157	    async def _post_request(self, payload: dict, endpoint: str, max_retries: int = 16):
158	        url = f"http://{self.reward_router_address}/{endpoint}"
159	        last_exception = None
160	        for attempt in range(max_retries):
161	            try:
162	                # It's safer to have a timeout instead of None, which can hang indefinitely.
163	                timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=None)
164	                async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=timeout) as session:
165	                    async with session.post(url, json=payload) as resp:
166	                        resp.raise_for_status()
167	                        return await resp.json()
168	            except aiohttp.ClientResponseError as e:
169	                # Do not retry on 4xx client errors, but retry on 5xx server errors.
170	                if 400 <= e.status < 500:
171	                    logger.error(f"Request to {url} failed with client error HTTP {e.status}: {e}. Not retrying.")
172	                    raise
173	                last_exception = e
174	                logger.warning(
175	                    f"[Attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_retries}] Request to {url} failed with HTTP {e.status}: {e}. "
176	                    "Retrying..."
177	                )
178	            except (asyncio.TimeoutError, aiohttp.ClientConnectorError) as e:
179	                last_exception = e
180	                logger.warning(f"[Attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_retries}] Request to {url} failed: {e}. Retrying...")
181	            except Exception as e:
182	                last_exception = e
183	                logger.warning(
184	                    f"[Attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_retries}] Request to {url} failed with unexpected error: {e}. "
185	                    "Retrying..."
186	                )
187	
188	            if attempt < max_retries - 1:
189	                # Using exponential backoff is generally better than a fixed sleep.
190	                backoff_seconds = 2**attempt
191	                await asyncio.sleep(min(backoff_seconds, 30))
192	
193	        logger.error(f"Max retries ({max_retries}) reached for request to {url}.")
194	        if last_exception:
195	            raise last_exception
196	
197	    async def _preprocess_reward_inputs(self, data: DataProto) -> str:
198	        assert len(data) == 1, "RewardLoopWorker only support single data item"
199	        data_item = data[0]
200	        assert "raw_prompt" in data_item.non_tensor_batch
201	
202	        # extract raw prompt
203	        chat: list = list(data_item.non_tensor_batch["raw_prompt"])
204	
205	        # extract response
206	        response_ids = data_item.batch["responses"]
207	        response_length = response_ids.shape[-1]
208	        valid_response_length = data_item.batch["attention_mask"][-response_length:].sum()
209	        valid_response_ids = response_ids[:valid_response_length]
210	
211	        rollout_response = self.input_tokenizer.decode(valid_response_ids)
212	        rollout_response = rollout_response.replace(self.input_tokenizer.eos_token, "")
213	
214	        chat.append({"role": "assistant", "content": rollout_response})
215	
216	        rm_prompt = self.reward_model_tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
217	            chat,
218	            add_generation_prompt=False,
219	            tokenize=False,
220	        )
221	
222	        # llama tokenizer will add bos token by default
223	        # will be removed in vllm >= 0.11.2, where we can add "add_special_tokens" = False
224	        if self.reward_model_tokenizer.bos_token is not None and rm_prompt.startswith(
225	            self.reward_model_tokenizer.bos_token
226	        ):
227	            rm_prompt = rm_prompt[len(self.reward_model_tokenizer.bos_token) :]
228	
229	        return rm_prompt
230	
231	    async def compute_score_disrm(self, data: DataProto) -> dict:
232	        disrm_prompt = await self._preprocess_reward_inputs(data)
233	        engine_name = self.config.reward.reward_model.rollout.name
234	        model_name = self.config.reward.reward_model.model_path
235	        if engine_name == "vllm":
236	            payloads = {
237	                "model": model_name,
238	                "input": disrm_prompt,
239	                "use_activation": False,
240	            }
241	            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "classify")
242	            rm_score = output["data"][-1]["probs"][-1]
243	        elif engine_name == "sglang":
244	            payloads = {
245	                "model": model_name,
246	                "input": disrm_prompt,
247	            }
248	            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "v1/embeddings")
249	            rm_score = output["data"][-1]["embedding"][-1]
250	        elif engine_name == "trtllm":
251	            # TODO: remove this once TRT-LLM switches to TorchSampler
252	            raise ValueError("TensorRT-LLM backend does not support reward models currently.")
253	
254	            payloads = {
255	                "model": model_name,
256	                "prompt": disrm_prompt,
257	                "return_context_logits": True,
258	            }
259	            output = await self._post_request(payloads, "v1/completions")
260	            rm_score = output["choices"][0]["context_logits"]
261	            assert isinstance(rm_score, list) and len(rm_score) > 0, (
262	                "TensorRT-LLM OpenAI server response for reward score is not in the expected format."
263	            )
264	
265	            rm_score = float(rm_score[0][0])
266	            logger.debug(f"rm score: {rm_score}")
267	        else:
268	            raise NotImplementedError(f"RewardLoopManager does not support {engine_name}")
269	
270	        return {"reward_score": rm_score}

273	class RewardLoopManager:
274	    """
275	    RewardLoopManager run in single controller.
276	    This class will create reward loop workers and manage them.
277	    """
278	
279	    def __init__(self, config: DictConfig, rm_resource_pool: RayResourcePool = None):
280	        self.config = config
281	        if self.config.reward.reward_model.enable:
282	            rm_rollout = self.config.reward.reward_model.rollout
283	            # The discriminative /classify (pooling) path is not covered by
284	            # VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT (vLLM batch invariance is verified on generation
285	            # models, not pooling RM architectures). Serialize /classify with
286	            # max_num_seqs=1 to keep it bitwise reproducible. The generative
287	            # /v1/chat/completions path (custom reward fn) is user-managed and not
288	            # forced here — rely on VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT + per-request seed.
289	            if (
290	                rm_rollout.full_determinism
291	                and self.config.reward.custom_reward_function.path is None
292	                and rm_rollout.max_num_seqs != 1
293	            ):
294	                logger.warning(
295	                    "[reward_model] full_determinism=True: forcing rollout.max_num_seqs "
296	                    "from %s to 1 for the /classify pooling path (batch invariance not "
297	                    "verified for pooling RM). See the determinism doc.",
298	                    rm_rollout.max_num_seqs,
299	                )
300	                with open_dict(self.config):
301	                    rm_rollout.max_num_seqs = 1
302	            self.reward_model_manager = RewardModelManager(config.reward.reward_model, rm_resource_pool)
303	            self.reward_router_address = self.reward_model_manager.get_router_address()
304	        else:
305	            self.reward_model_manager = None
306	            self.reward_router_address = None
307	
308	        self.reward_loop_workers_class = ray.remote(RewardLoopWorker)
309	        self.reward_manager_cls = resolve_reward_manager_cls(config)
310	        self._init_reward_loop_workers()
311	
312	    @property
313	    def reward_loop_worker_handles(self) -> list[ActorHandle]:
314	        """Return worker handles for agent loop worker to compute reward score.
315	
316	        Only return worker handles when reward computation can be parallelized with rollout:
317	        (1) rule-based reward without reward model
318	        (2) reward model with extra resource pool
319	        """
320	        if not self.config.reward.reward_model.enable or self.config.reward.reward_model.enable_resource_pool:
321	            return self.reward_loop_workers
322	        return None
323	
324	    def _init_reward_loop_workers(self):
325	        self.reward_loop_workers = []
326	        num_workers = self.config.reward.num_workers
327	        node_ids = [node["NodeID"] for node in ray.nodes() if node["Alive"] and node["Resources"].get("CPU", 0) > 0]
328	
329	        for i in range(num_workers):
330	            # Round-robin scheduling over the all nodes
331	            node_id = node_ids[i % len(node_ids)]
332	
333	            self.reward_loop_workers.append(
334	                self.reward_loop_workers_class.options(
335	                    name=f"reward_loop_worker_{i}",
336	                    scheduling_strategy=ray.util.scheduling_strategies.NodeAffinitySchedulingStrategy(
337	                        node_id=node_id,
338	                        soft=True,
339	                    ),
340	                ).remote(self.config, self.reward_router_address)
341	            )
342	
343	    def compute_rm_score(self, data: DataProto) -> DataProto:
344	        if self.reward_model_manager is not None:

from verl.utils.ray_utils import auto_await
from verl.utils.tensordict_utils import list_of_dict_to_tensordict

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
logger.setLevel(os.getenv("VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL", "INFO"))


def apply_greedy_sampling_params(params: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    params["top_p"] = 1.0
    params["top_k"] = -1
    params["temperature"] = 0


async def _settle_session_tasks(tasks: list[asyncio.Task[Any]]) -> list[BaseException]:
    results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
    return [result for result in results if isinstance(result, BaseException)]


@ray.remote
class AgentLoopWorkerTQ(AgentLoopWorker):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        tq.init()
        self.background_tasks = set()

    async def generate_sequences(self, batch: TensorDict) -> None:
        """Spawn agent loop for each sample in the batch without waiting for the results."""
        validate = batch["validate"] if "validate" in batch else False
        batch.pop("validate", None)
        config = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout
        sampling_params = dict(
            temperature=config.temperature,
            top_p=config.top_p,
            top_k=config.top_k,
            repetition_penalty=1.0,
            logprobs=config.calculate_log_probs,
        )

        # override sampling params for validation
        if validate:
            sampling_params["top_p"] = config.val_kwargs.top_p
            sampling_params["top_k"] = config.val_kwargs.top_k
            sampling_params["temperature"] = config.val_kwargs.temperature

        # by default, we assume it's a single turn agent
        if "agent_name" not in batch:
            default_agent_loop = config.agent.default_agent_loop
            batch["agent_name"] = NonTensorData(default_agent_loop)

        trajectory_info = await get_trajectory_info(batch["global_steps"], batch["index"], validate)

        # create background tasks for each sample in the batch
        for i in range(len(batch)):
            # TODO(wuxibin): add trace support
            trace_this_sample = False
            prompt = {}
            for k, v in batch.items():
                if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor):
                    prompt[k] = v[i]
                elif isinstance(v, NonTensorStack):
                    prompt[k] = v[i].data
                elif isinstance(v, NonTensorData):
                    prompt[k] = v.data
                else:
                    logger.exception(f"Unsupported type {type(v)} for key {k}")

            # “fire-and-forget” background tasks
            task = asyncio.create_task(
                self._run_prompt(prompt, sampling_params, trajectory=trajectory_info[i], trace=trace_this_sample)
            )
            self.background_tasks.add(task)
            task.add_done_callback(self.background_tasks.discard)

    async def _run_prompt(self, prompt: dict, sampling_params: dict, trajectory: dict, trace: bool = False) -> None:
        """Spawn multiple agent loops in parallel according to rollout.n or rollout.val_kwargs.n."""
        uid, partition_id = prompt["uid"], "train" if not trajectory["validate"] else "val"
        await tq.async_kv_put(key=uid, partition_id=partition_id, tag={"status": "running"})
        tasks = []
        try:
            # NOTE: user can dynamically adjust n for each sample here, e.g according to task difficulty.
            config = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout
            n = prompt.pop("__rollout_n__", config.n if not trajectory["validate"] else config.val_kwargs.n)
            do_sample = prompt.pop("__do_sample__", True)

            run_sampling_params = dict(sampling_params)
            if not trajectory["validate"] and not do_sample:
                apply_greedy_sampling_params(run_sampling_params)

            tasks = []
            for i in range(n):
                task = asyncio.create_task(
                    self._run_agent_loop(
                        run_sampling_params, trajectory=trajectory, trace=trace, session_id=i, **prompt
                    )
                )
                tasks.append(task)

            # Publish a terminal status only after every session settles, so no sibling can write after
            # ReplayBuffer clears a failed group.
            session_errors = await _settle_session_tasks(tasks)
            if session_errors:
                for error in session_errors:
                    logger.error(
                        f"Error in _run_prompt for uid={uid}",
                        exc_info=(type(error), error, error.__traceback__),
                    )
                status = "failure"
            else:
                status = "finished"
            await tq.async_kv_put(key=uid, partition_id=partition_id, tag={"status": status})
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception(f"Error in _run_prompt: {e}")
            if tasks:
                await _settle_session_tasks(tasks)
            await tq.async_kv_put(key=uid, partition_id=partition_id, tag={"status": "failure"})

116	    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
117	        """Convert agent loop output to a dictionary."""
118	        output = self.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
119	
120	        output["prompts"] = torch.tensor(output.pop("prompt_ids"), dtype=torch.int64)
121	        output["responses"] = torch.tensor(output.pop("response_ids"), dtype=torch.int64)
122	        output["response_mask"] = torch.tensor(output.pop("response_mask"), dtype=torch.int64)
123	
124	        response_logprobs = output.pop("response_logprobs", None)
125	        if response_logprobs is not None:
126	            output["rollout_log_probs"] = torch.tensor(response_logprobs, dtype=torch.float32)
127	
128	        routed_experts = output.pop("routed_experts", None)
129	        if routed_experts is not None:
130	            routed_experts = torch.tensor(routed_experts, dtype=torch.int64)
131	            # Router replay indexes this field by absolute token position, so it must
132	            # span the whole sequence. The rollout engine records fewer rows than that:
133	            # it only sees tokens fed through the model, and multi-turn loops stop
134	            # recording at the last generation. Trailing rows stay zero; replay masks
135	            # them out instead of consuming them.
136	            total_length = output["prompts"].size(0) + output["responses"].size(0)
137	            aligned = routed_experts.new_zeros((total_length, *routed_experts.shape[1:]))
138	            num_rows = min(routed_experts.size(0), total_length)
139	            aligned[:num_rows] = routed_experts[:num_rows]
140	            output["routed_experts"] = aligned
141	
142	        # rm_scores: reward score for each token
143	        reward_score = output.pop("reward_score", None)
144	        if reward_score is not None:
145	            rm_scores = torch.zeros_like(output["response_mask"], dtype=torch.float32)
146	            rm_scores[-1] = reward_score
147	            output["rm_scores"] = rm_scores
148	
149	        teacher_ids, teacher_logprobs = (
150	            output["extra_fields"].pop("teacher_ids", None),
151	            output["extra_fields"].pop("teacher_logprobs", None),
152	        )
153	        if teacher_ids is not None:
154	            output["teacher_ids"] = teacher_ids
155	        if teacher_logprobs is not None:
156	            output["teacher_logprobs"] = teacher_logprobs
157	        return output

def rearrange_micro_batches(
    batch,
    max_token_len,
    dp_group=None,
    num_batches_divided_by=None,
    same_micro_num_in_dp=True,
    min_num_micro_batch=None,
    use_dynamic_bsz_balance=True,
    force_group_size=1,
):
    """
    Split a batch into micro-batches by total token count, with optional DP sync and padding.

    Args:
        batch (TensorDict): must include "attention_mask" (B*S); other fields are sliced similarly.
        max_token_len (int): max sum of attention_mask per micro-batch.
        dp_group (optional): torch.distributed group for data-parallel sync.
        num_batches_divided_by (optional): virtual pipeline parallel size, for megatron.
        same_micro_num_in_dp (bool): if True and dp_group set, pad all ranks to the same count.
        min_num_micro_batch (int, optional): force at least this many splits (pads empty ones).
        use_dynamic_bsz_balance (bool, optional): balance the computational workload between micro-batches
        force_group_size (int, optional): force consecutive samples to be in the same micro-batch (for RM training).

    Returns:
        List[TensorDict]: the micro-batches.
        List[List[int]]: index lists mapping each micro-batch back to original positions.
    """
    # this is per local micro_bsz
    input_ids = batch["input_ids"]
    if input_ids.is_nested:
        seq_len_effective: torch.Tensor = input_ids.offsets().diff()
        max_seq_len = max(seq_len_effective)
    else:
        max_seq_len = batch["attention_mask"].shape[-1]
        seq_len_effective: torch.Tensor = batch["attention_mask"].sum(dim=1)

    assert max_token_len >= max_seq_len, (
        f"max_token_len must be greater than the sequence length. Got {max_token_len=} and {max_seq_len=}"
    )

    # Validate force_group_size
    batch_size = len(seq_len_effective)
    assert batch_size % force_group_size == 0, (
        f"Batch size {batch_size} must be divisible by force_group_size {force_group_size}"
    )

    total_seqlen = seq_len_effective.sum().item()
    # NOTE: num_microbatches <= batch_size, so take the min of this two.
    # When force_group_size > 1, we work with groups instead of individual samples
    num_groups = batch_size // force_group_size
    num_micro_batches = min(num_groups, ceildiv(total_seqlen, max_token_len))
    if min_num_micro_batch is not None:
        # used to support pp
        num_micro_batches = max(min_num_micro_batch, num_micro_batches)
    if dist.is_initialized() and same_micro_num_in_dp and dp_group is not None:
        num_micro_batches = torch.tensor([num_micro_batches], device=get_device_name())
        dist.all_reduce(num_micro_batches, op=dist.ReduceOp.MAX, group=dp_group)
        num_micro_batches = num_micro_batches.cpu().item()
    if num_batches_divided_by is not None:
        num_micro_batches = roundup_divisible(num_micro_batches, num_batches_divided_by)

    assert num_micro_batches <= num_groups

    # upcast to int64 to avoid potential overflow im `calculate_workload` computation.
    seq_len_effective = seq_len_effective.long()

    # When force_group_size > 1, aggregate workloads by groups
    if force_group_size > 1:
        # Calculate workload for each group (sum of workloads of samples in the group)
        workloads_per_sample = calculate_workload(seq_len_effective)
        workloads_per_sample_grouped = workloads_per_sample.view(num_groups, force_group_size)
        group_workloads = workloads_per_sample_grouped.sum(dim=1).cpu().tolist()

        # Partition groups instead of individual samples
        micro_bsz_group_idx = get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(group_workloads, num_micro_batches, equal_size=False)

        # Convert group indices back to sample indices
        micro_bsz_idx = []
        for group_partition in micro_bsz_group_idx:
            sample_partition = []
            for group_idx in group_partition:
                start_idx = group_idx * force_group_size
                sample_partition.extend(range(start_idx, start_idx + force_group_size))
            micro_bsz_idx.append(sample_partition)

        workloads = group_workloads
    else:
        # Original logic for force_group_size == 1
        # note that seq_len_effective is a GPU tensor. We need to make it a list to avoid D2H!
        workloads = calculate_workload(seq_len_effective).cpu().tolist()
        micro_bsz_idx = get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(workloads, num_micro_batches, equal_size=False)

    if use_dynamic_bsz_balance:
        # Use the sum of squared sequence lengths to approximate attention computation workload
        if force_group_size > 1:
            # For grouped samples, use group workloads for sorting
            micro_bsz_idx.sort(
                key=lambda partition: (
                    sum(workloads[idx // force_group_size] for idx in partition[::force_group_size]),
                    partition[0] if partition else 0,
                ),
                reverse=True,
            )
        else:
            micro_bsz_idx.sort(
                key=lambda partition: (
                    sum(workloads[idx] for idx in partition),
                    partition[0] if partition else 0,
                ),
                reverse=True,
            )
        # Place smaller micro-batches at both ends to reduce the bubbles exposed during the warm-up and cool-down.
        micro_bsz_idx = micro_bsz_idx[::2][::-1] + micro_bsz_idx[1::2]

    micro_batches = []

    for partition in micro_bsz_idx:
        curr_micro_batch = tu.index_select_tensor_dict(batch, partition)
        micro_batches.append(curr_micro_batch)

    return micro_batches, micro_bsz_idx

93	def qwen2_5_vl_dedup_image_tokens(prompt_ids: list[int], processor):
94	    """Deduplicate consecutive image tokens in prompt_ids for Qwen2.5-VL, since vLLM will replicate the
95	    <|image_pad|> and <|video_pad|> token by image_data.
96	    For example,
97	    ```
98	    <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|image_pad|>...<|image_pad|><|vision_end|>
99	    =>
100	    <|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>
101	    ```
102	    """
103	    if (
104	        processor is not None
105	        and hasattr(processor, "image_processor")
106	        and "Qwen2VLImageProcessor" in processor.image_processor.__class__.__name__
107	    ):
108	        prompt_ids = np.array(prompt_ids)
109	        mask = np.ones(len(prompt_ids), dtype=bool)
110	        is_value = (prompt_ids == processor.image_token_id) | (prompt_ids == processor.video_token_id)
111	        mask[1:] &= ~(is_value[1:] & is_value[:-1])
112	        return prompt_ids[mask].tolist()
113	    else:
114	        return prompt_ids

117	def get_vision_placeholder_token_ids(processor) -> list[int]:
118	    """Vision placeholder token ids the policy must never sample.
119	
120	    An `<|image_pad|>` or `<|video_pad|>` token only means something when a real image or video
121	    sits behind it: the k-th run of placeholders pairs with the k-th row of `image_grid_thw` /
122	    `video_grid_thw`. Nothing stops the policy from sampling one anyway -- it is an ordinary entry
123	    of the vocabulary -- and then that pairing silently breaks. Every downstream consumer trusts
124	    it, so each one has its own way of dying: `get_rope_index` walks off the end of the grid
125	    iterator, and `merge_multimodal_embeddings` scatters into a mask that no longer matches the
126	    embedding count. Both take the whole training job down with them.
127	
128	    A tool that returns an image is unaffected: that image arrives in the next turn's prompt, not
129	    in what the model generates.
130	
131	    Returns an empty list for text-only models, leaving sampling untouched.
132	    """
133	    token_ids = []
134	    for modality in ("image", "video"):
135	        token_id = get_processor_token_id(processor, modality)
136	        if token_id is not None:
137	            token_ids.append(token_id)
138	    return token_ids

19	from verl.utils import tensordict_utils as tu
20	from verl.utils.attention_utils import index_first_axis, unpad_input

23	def left_right_2_no_padding(data: TensorDict) -> TensorDict:
24	    """
25	    Convert TensorDict from left-right padding to no-padding format.
26	
27	    Args:
28	        data: TensorDict with "input_ids", "attention_mask", "response_mask", "position_ids"
29	
30	    Returns:
31	        data: TensorDict with
32	        - Tensor includes NestedTensors like "input_ids", "loss_mask", "position_ids"
33	        - NonTensorData includes "max_seq_len", "max_response_len", "indices"
34	
35	    Note:
36	    1. the return input_ids/position_ids/loss_mask are nested tensor.
37	    2. we will remove "attention_mask", "response" in the return data, but "response_mask" is kept.
38	    """
39	    assert "input_ids" in data, "input_ids is required in left-right padding data"
40	    assert "attention_mask" in data, "attention_mask is required in left-right padding data"
41	    assert "response_mask" in data, "response_mask is required in left-right padding data"
42	    assert "position_ids" in data, "position_ids is required in left-right padding data"
43	
44	    input_ids = data.pop("input_ids")
45	    attention_mask = data["attention_mask"]
46	    response_mask = data["response_mask"]
47	    position_ids = data["position_ids"]  # (bs, seq_len) or # (bs, 4, seq_len)
48	
49	    max_seq_len, max_response_len = input_ids.shape[1], response_mask.shape[1]
50	    tu.assign_non_tensor_data(data, "max_seq_len", max_seq_len)
51	    tu.assign_non_tensor_data(data, "max_response_len", max_response_len)
52	
53	    input_ids_rmpad, indices, cu_seqlens, *_ = unpad_input(input_ids.unsqueeze(-1), attention_mask)
54	    tu.assign_non_tensor_data(data, "indices", indices)
55	
56	    input_ids_nested = torch.nested.nested_tensor_from_jagged(input_ids_rmpad.squeeze(-1), offsets=cu_seqlens)
57	
58	    position_ids_list = []
59	    for i in range(attention_mask.shape[0]):
60	        curr_mask = attention_mask[i].bool()
61	        curr_pos_ids = position_ids[i]
62	        if curr_pos_ids.dim() == 1:  # (seq_len,)
63	            valid_ids = curr_pos_ids[curr_mask]
64	        else:  # (4, seq_len)
65	            valid_ids = curr_pos_ids[:, curr_mask]
66	        position_ids_list.append(valid_ids)
67	    position_ids_nested = torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(position_ids_list, layout=torch.jagged)
68	
69	    data["input_ids"] = input_ids_nested
70	    data["position_ids"] = position_ids_nested
71	    data["loss_mask"] = data["response_mask"]
72	
73	    routed_experts = data.get("routed_experts", None)
74	    if routed_experts is not None and not routed_experts.is_nested:
75	        if routed_experts.max() <= 255:
76	            routed_experts = routed_experts.to(torch.uint8)
77	        routed_experts_rmpad = index_first_axis(routed_experts.unsqueeze(-1).flatten(0, 1), indices)
78	        routed_experts_nested = torch.nested.nested_tensor_from_jagged(
79	            routed_experts_rmpad.squeeze(-1), offsets=cu_seqlens
80	        )
81	        data["routed_experts"] = routed_experts_nested
82	
83	    # (bsz, seqlen, topk)
84	    teacher_logprobs = data.get("teacher_logprobs", None)
85	    teacher_ids = data.get("teacher_ids", None)
86	    if teacher_logprobs is not None and teacher_ids is not None:
87	        teacher_logprobs_rmpad = index_first_axis(teacher_logprobs.unsqueeze(-1).flatten(0, 1), indices)
88	        teacher_ids_rmpad = index_first_axis(teacher_ids.unsqueeze(-1).flatten(0, 1), indices)
89	        teacher_logprobs_nested = torch.nested.nested_tensor_from_jagged(
90	            teacher_logprobs_rmpad.squeeze(-1), offsets=cu_seqlens
91	        )
92	        teacher_ids_nested = torch.nested.nested_tensor_from_jagged(teacher_ids_rmpad.squeeze(-1), offsets=cu_seqlens)
93	        data["teacher_logprobs"] = teacher_logprobs_nested
94	        data["teacher_ids"] = teacher_ids_nested
95	
96	    return data
97	
98	
99	def no_padding_2_padding(tensor: torch.Tensor, data: TensorDict) -> torch.Tensor:
100	    """Slice response from unpad model output.
101	
102	    Args:
103	        tensor: a nested tensor or a tensor of shape (total_nnz,*),
104	            total_nnz is the total number of tokens across all sequences in the batch
105	
106	        data: TensorDict with "prompts", "responses", "attention_mask"
107	
108	    Returns:
109	        tensor: sliced response tensor of shape [bsz, max_response_len, *]
110	    """
111	    values = tensor.values() if tensor.is_nested else tensor
112	    prompt_ids = data["prompts"]
113	    response_ids = data["responses"]
114	
115	    max_response_len = tu.get_non_tensor_data(data=data, key="max_response_len", default=-1)
116	
117	    if prompt_ids.is_nested:
118	        prompt_lens = prompt_ids.offsets().diff()
119	        response_lens = response_ids.offsets().diff()
120	        if max_response_len < 0:
121	            max_response_len = response_lens.max().item()
122	    else:
123	        attention_mask = data["attention_mask"]
124	        assert not attention_mask.is_nested
125	        prompt_lens = attention_mask[:, : prompt_ids.shape[1]].sum(dim=1)
126	        response_lens = attention_mask[:, prompt_ids.shape[1] :].sum(dim=1)
127	        max_response_len = response_ids.shape[1]
128	
129	    sequence_lens = prompt_lens + response_lens
130	    sequence_offsets = sequence_lens.cumsum(dim=0)
131	    assert sequence_offsets[-1].item() == values.shape[0]
132	    assert not prompt_lens.eq(0).any(), f"seq_offset - resp_len - 1 assumes prompt_len > 0. Got {prompt_lens}"
133	
134	    response_list = []
135	    # Skip padding dimensions after sequence dimensions, if any.
136	    skip_padding = (0, 0) * (values.ndim - 1)
137	    for resp_len, seq_offset in zip(response_lens, sequence_offsets, strict=True):
138	        pad_size = max_response_len - resp_len
139	        # left-shift model output by one token for log_probs/values
140	        response_list.append(F.pad(values[seq_offset - resp_len - 1 : seq_offset - 1], (*skip_padding, 0, pad_size)))
141	
142	    output = torch.stack(response_list, dim=0)
143	    return output
144	
145	
146	def build_attention_mask_from_nested(input_ids: torch.Tensor, max_seq_len: int | None = None) -> torch.Tensor:
147	    """Build a padded full-sequence attention mask from nested input ids."""
148	    assert input_ids.is_nested, "input_ids must be a nested tensor"
149	    device = input_ids.values().device
150	    seq_lens = input_ids.offsets().diff().to(device=device)
151	    if max_seq_len is None:
152	        max_seq_len = int(seq_lens.max().item())
153	    positions = torch.arange(max_seq_len, device=device).unsqueeze(0)
154	    return (positions < seq_lens.unsqueeze(1)).to(torch.int32)
155	
156	
157	def embeds_padding_2_no_padding(data: TensorDict) -> TensorDict:
158	    """
159	    Convert TensorDict from prompt embeds with padding to no-padding format.
160	
161	    Currently we expect the prompt embedding mask to be [1111000...] format,
162	    which means the valid tokens are continuous and start from the left.
163	
164	    Args:
165	        data: TensorDict with "prompt_embeds", "prompt_embeds_mask",
166	              "negative_prompt_embeds", "negative_prompt_embeds_mask"
167	
168	    Returns:
169	        data: TensorDict with
170	        - Tensor includes NestedTensors "prompt_embeds", "prompt_embeds_mask",
171	          "negative_prompt_embeds", "negative_prompt_embeds_mask"
172	    """
173	
174	    def _to_nested(embeds: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor):
175	        """Strip padding from (bs, seq_len, dim) embeds using the boolean mask and return nested tensors."""
176	        embeds_list, mask_list = [], []
177	        for i in range(mask.shape[0]):
178	            curr_mask = mask[i].bool()
179	            embeds_list.append(embeds[i, curr_mask, :])
180	            mask_list.append(curr_mask[curr_mask])
181	        return (
182	            torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(embeds_list, layout=torch.jagged),
183	            torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(mask_list, layout=torch.jagged),
184	        )
185	
186	    data["prompt_embeds"], data["prompt_embeds_mask"] = _to_nested(data["prompt_embeds"], data["prompt_embeds_mask"])
187	
188	    if isinstance(data.get("negative_prompt_embeds", None), torch.Tensor):
189	        data["negative_prompt_embeds"], data["negative_prompt_embeds_mask"] = _to_nested(
190	            data["negative_prompt_embeds"], data["negative_prompt_embeds_mask"]
191	        )
192	
193	    return data
194	
195	
196	def response_from_nested(tensor: torch.Tensor, response_mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
197	    """Extract response from nested model output.
198	
199	    Args:
200	        tensor: a nested tensor with shape (bsz, prompt_len + response_len)
201	        response_mask: a nested tensor with shape (bsz, response_len)
202	
203	    Returns:
204	        tensor: a nested tensor with shape (bsz, response_len)
205	    """
206	    values, offsets = tensor.values(), tensor.offsets()
207	    response_lens = response_mask.offsets().diff()
208	    response_list = []
209	    for resp_len, seq_offset in zip(response_lens, offsets[1:], strict=True):
210	        # left-shift model output by one token for log_probs/values
211	        response_list.append(values[seq_offset - resp_len - 1 : seq_offset - 1])
212	    return torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(response_list, layout=torch.jagged)
213	
214	
215	def response_to_nested(tensor: torch.Tensor, response_mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
216	    """Convert padded response tensor to nested tensor.
217	
218	    Args:
219	        tensor: a tensor with shape (bsz, response_len)
220	        response_mask: a nested tensor with shape (bsz, response_len)
221	
222	    Returns:
223	        tensor: a nested tensor with shape (bsz, response_len)
224	    """
225	    assert response_mask.is_nested
226	    response_lens = response_mask.offsets().diff()
227	    response_list = []
228	    for i in range(tensor.shape[0]):
229	        response_list.append(tensor[i, : response_lens[i]])
230	
231	    return torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(response_list, layout=torch.jagged)

15	
16	import torch
17	from tensordict import TensorDict
18	
19	from verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos import agg_loss, compute_value_loss, get_policy_loss_fn, kl_penalty
20	from verl.utils import tensordict_utils as tu
21	from verl.utils.dataset.dataset_utils import DatasetPadMode
22	from verl.utils.metric import AggregationType, Metric
23	from verl.utils.torch_functional import masked_mean, masked_sum
24	from verl.workers.config import ActorConfig, CriticConfig
25	from verl.workers.utils.padding import no_padding_2_padding
26	
27	
28	def sft_loss(config: ActorConfig, model_output, data: TensorDict, dp_group=None):
29	    pad_mode = tu.get_non_tensor_data(data=data, key="pad_mode", default=DatasetPadMode.NO_PADDING)
30	    dp_size = data["dp_size"]
31	    batch_num_tokens = data["batch_num_tokens"]
32	
33	    log_prob = model_output["log_probs"]
34	
35	    if pad_mode == DatasetPadMode.NO_PADDING:
36	        # log_prob and loss mask are nested tensors of shape [bsz, j1]
37	        # for each sample, loss mask shape is [1, prompt_length + response_length]
38	        loss_mask = data["loss_mask"]
39	
40	        log_prob_flatten = log_prob.values()
41	        loss_mask_flatten = loss_mask.values()
42	
43	        # left-shift the loss mask by one token to align with log_prob
44	        loss_mask_flatten = torch.roll(loss_mask_flatten, shifts=-1, dims=0)
45	
46	        # NOTE: loss is averaged over all tokens in the batch across all data parallel groups,
47	        # For FSDP backend, the loss is directly used for backward; while for Megatron backend,
48	        # the loss should be scaled by `num_microbatches` for pp schedule.
49	        loss = -masked_sum(log_prob_flatten, loss_mask_flatten) / batch_num_tokens * dp_size
50	    else:
51	        response_mask = data["response_mask"].to(bool)
52	        loss = -masked_sum(log_prob, response_mask) / batch_num_tokens * dp_size
53	
54	    return loss, {}
55	
56	
57	def ppo_loss(config: ActorConfig, model_output, data: TensorDict, dp_group=None):
58	    """Computes ppo loss from model output (log_prob, entropy, values, etc. ) and old_log_probs from data."""
59	    log_prob = no_padding_2_padding(model_output["log_probs"], data)
60	    entropy = model_output.get("entropy", None)
61	    if entropy is not None:
62	        entropy = no_padding_2_padding(entropy, data)
63	
64	    # global batch info for loss aggregation
65	    config.global_batch_info["dp_size"] = data["dp_size"]
66	    config.global_batch_info["batch_num_tokens"] = data["batch_num_tokens"]
67	    config.global_batch_info["global_batch_size"] = data["global_batch_size"]
68	    config.global_batch_info["loss_scale_factor"] = config.loss_scale_factor
69	
70	    # assumes that if any of the global batch info is set, the policy_loss_fn will
71	    # normalize using dp_size/global_bsz/global_token; in this case, metric aggregation should be SUM
72	    # to reflect the mean loss over the global batch
73	    if (
74	        data["dp_size"] > 1
75	        or data["batch_num_tokens"] is not None
76	        or data["global_batch_size"] is not None
77	        or config.loss_scale_factor is not None
78	    ):
79	        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.SUM
80	    else:
81	        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.MEAN
82	
83	    metrics = {}
84	
85	    # select fields and convert to padded tensor
86	    fields = ["response_mask", "old_log_probs", "advantages"]
87	    if "rollout_is_weights" in data:
88	        fields.append("rollout_is_weights")
89	    if "ref_log_prob" in data:
90	        fields.append("ref_log_prob")
91	    data = data.select(*fields).to_padded_tensor()
92	
93	    response_mask = data["response_mask"].to(bool)
94	    # compute policy loss
95	    old_log_prob = data["old_log_probs"]
96	    advantages = data["advantages"]
97	    rollout_is_weights = data.get("rollout_is_weights", None)
98	
99	    loss_agg_mode = config.loss_agg_mode
100	
101	    loss_mode = config.policy_loss.get("loss_mode", "vanilla")
102	
103	    policy_loss_fn = get_policy_loss_fn(loss_mode)
104	    pg_loss, pg_metrics = policy_loss_fn(
105	        old_log_prob=old_log_prob,
106	        log_prob=log_prob,
107	        advantages=advantages,
108	        response_mask=response_mask,
109	        loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode,
110	        config=config,
111	        rollout_is_weights=rollout_is_weights,
112	    )
113	
114	    # AggregationType.MEAN for pg metrics: assumes policy_loss_fn normalizes by local_bsz/local_tokens
115	    # Ex: in compute_policy_loss_vanilla, pg_metrics are pg_clipfrac, ppo_kl, pg_clipfrac_lower
116	    pg_metrics = Metric.from_dict(pg_metrics, aggregation=AggregationType.MEAN)
117	
118	    metrics.update(pg_metrics)
119	    metrics["actor/pg_loss"] = Metric(value=pg_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)
120	    policy_loss = pg_loss
121	
122	    # add entropy loss
123	    if entropy is not None:
124	        entropy_loss = agg_loss(
125	            loss_mat=entropy, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
126	        )
127	        entropy_coeff = config.entropy_coeff
128	        policy_loss -= entropy_coeff * entropy_loss
129	        metrics["actor/entropy_loss"] = Metric(value=entropy_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)
130	
131	    # add kl loss
132	    if config.use_kl_loss:
133	        ref_log_prob = data["ref_log_prob"]
134	        # compute kl loss
135	        kld = kl_penalty(logprob=log_prob, ref_logprob=ref_log_prob, kl_penalty=config.kl_loss_type)
136	        kl_loss = agg_loss(
137	            loss_mat=kld, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=config.loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
138	        )
139	
140	        policy_loss += kl_loss * config.kl_loss_coef
141	        metrics["kl_loss"] = Metric(value=kl_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)
142	        metrics["kl_coef"] = config.kl_loss_coef
143	
144	    return policy_loss, metrics
145	
146	
147	def value_loss(config: CriticConfig, model_output, data: TensorDict, dp_group=None):
148	    """value loss
149	
150	    Args:
151	        config: CriticConfig
152	        model_output: model output from the model
153	        data: the input to the model
154	        dp_group: data paralle group
155	
156	    Returns:
157	        value loss
158	    """
159	    vpreds = no_padding_2_padding(model_output["values"], data)  # (bsz, response_length)
160	
161	    # Normalize the value loss over the global mini-batch (dp_size / batch_num_tokens /
162	    # global_batch_size) instead of the local micro-batch, so the accumulated critic gradient is
163	    # invariant to how the mini-batch is split into micro-batches (as the actor's ppo_loss does).
164	    dp_size = data["dp_size"]
165	    batch_num_tokens = data["batch_num_tokens"]
166	    global_batch_size = data["global_batch_size"]
167	
168	    # When the loss is normalized over the global batch, each micro-batch contributes a partial sum,
169	    # so the loss metric must be aggregated with SUM to reflect the global-batch mean.
170	    if (
171	        dp_size > 1
172	        or batch_num_tokens is not None
173	        or global_batch_size is not None
174	        or config.loss_scale_factor is not None
175	    ):
176	        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.SUM
177	    else:
178	        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.MEAN
179	
180	    # select fields and convert to padded tensor
181	    data = data.select("values", "returns", "response_mask").to_padded_tensor()
182	    values = data["values"]
183	    returns = data["returns"]
184	    response_mask = data["response_mask"].to(bool)
185	
186	    vf_loss, vf_clipfrac = compute_value_loss(
187	        vpreds=vpreds,
188	        values=values,
189	        returns=returns,
190	        response_mask=response_mask,
191	        cliprange_value=config.cliprange_value,
192	        loss_agg_mode=config.loss_agg_mode,
193	        dp_size=dp_size,
194	        batch_num_tokens=batch_num_tokens,
195	        global_batch_size=global_batch_size,
196	        loss_scale_factor=config.loss_scale_factor,
197	    )
198	
199	    metrics = {
200	        "critic/vf_loss": Metric(value=vf_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation),
201	        "critic/vf_clipfrac": vf_clipfrac.detach().item(),
202	        "critic/vpred_mean": masked_mean(vpreds, response_mask).detach().item(),
203	    }
204	
205	    return vf_loss, metrics
206

22	def process_image(image: dict | Image.Image, image_patch_size: int = 14) -> Image.Image:
23	    from qwen_vl_utils import fetch_image
24	
25	    if isinstance(image, Image.Image):
26	        return image.convert("RGB")

32	    try:
