# Review of the staged GRPO run — Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct / geometry3k / verl 0.9.0 (FSDP2 + vLLM, 8 GPUs)

**Verdict: the experiment is healthy. No defect was found in the staged workspace, so no files were changed.**

Training was **not** launched at any point during this review (only reads of the recorded logs, hash checks of the
staged assets, code inspection/diffs against the HF reference, and CPU-only unit tests were run).

---

## 1. Root cause

### 1.1 Conclusion

There is no defect to attribute. Every signal that could indicate an unhealthy post-training run — held-out
accuracy, rollout statistics, truncation, runtime/memory, optimization statistics, and the engine-mismatch
diagnostics — is consistent with a correctly configured GRPO run operating inside a very small budget
(20 steps × 32 prompts × 5 samples, lr 1e-6, KL-regularised toward the reference). Several settings look
unusual at first glance; each one was traced to the observed behaviour and shown **not** to be causing
any degradation (section 1.4).

### 1.2 Held-out evidence (the primary signal)

Greedy, n=1 evaluation on the full 601-sample held-out split (`logs/recorded_run/validation/{0,5,10,15,20}.jsonl`,
`val-core/hiyouga/geometry3k/acc/mean@1` in `metrics.json`):

| step | val-core acc/mean@1 (reward) | accuracy (score > 0.5) |
|-----:|-----------------------------:|-----------------------:|
| 0    | 0.5136 | 57.07 % |
| 5    | 0.5511 | 61.23 % |
| 10   | 0.5241 | 58.24 % |
| 15   | 0.5286 | 58.74 % |
| 20   | 0.5316 | 59.07 % |

* Every post-training evaluation is **at or above** the step-0 baseline (+1.2 … +4.2 points). With 601 samples
  the standard error of one accuracy estimate is ≈ 2.0 points, so the trajectory is "flat-to-slightly-up,
  within noise" — there is no held-out degradation, collapse, or divergence between training reward and held-out
  accuracy.
* Paired analysis (the sanitized validation dumps have no outputs and their uids change every run, so samples
  were matched across runs on the 194 ground-truth strings that are unique in the test set): step 0 → 20 flips
  14 wrong→right vs 18 right→wrong (net −4/194 ≈ −2 points; two-sided sign test p ≈ 0.6). Per-interval churn is
  10–16 % of paired samples in both directions, which is the normal sensitivity of long greedy chains of reasoning
  to small weight updates, not a systematic drift.
* The validation reward values are exactly {0, 0.9}: `geo3k.compute_score = 0.9·acc + 0.1·format`, and the
  Instruct model never emits the `<think>…</think>` block demanded by the prompt, so the 0.1 format bonus is
  never earned by any sample at any step. This is identical to the upstream geo3k recipe and is not a grader
  fault (the grader file is byte-identical in behaviour to upstream: `mathruler.extract_boxed_content` +
  `grade_answer`, dispatched from `verl/utils/reward_score/__init__.py:89-92`).

### 1.3 Training-side evidence (all consistent with health)

Per-step values from `logs/recorded_run/metrics.json` (21 records):

* **Training reward (sampled, T=1.0, n=5)**: `critic/score/mean` 0.399 → 0.489 / 0.473 / 0.461 (steps 1–4, mean
  0.456) → 0.720 / 0.608 / 0.461 / 0.568 / 0.591 (steps 16–20, mean 0.590). The ≈ +13-point gain is the expected
  on-policy sharpening (sampled accuracy moving toward the greedy accuracy) plus the reduction in truncated,
  zero-reward samples; it is not a sign of reward hacking (reward is exact-answer matching, format bonus never
  triggered, no `<think>` tag gaming possible).
* **Response length / truncation**: mean response length 3067 tokens (step 1) → ≈ 2290 (steps 16–20);
  `response_length/clip_ratio` (truncated at 8192) 0.113 at step 1, peak 0.156 at step 8, 0.050–0.081 over steps
  16–20. Truncation is modest, trends downward, and `max_model_len = 10240 = 2048 + 8192` is exactly the prompt +
  response budget, so no generation is cut by the engine limit rather than by `max_response_length`.
* **Optimization**: `actor/grad_norm` 0.29–0.73 (clip 1.0 never saturating), `actor/pg_clipfrac` ≤ 7e-4,
  `actor/ppo_kl` ≈ ±1e-4 (two optimizer updates per step on fresh samples ⇒ nearly on-policy), `actor/kl_loss`
  (low_var_kl to the frozen reference, coef 0.01) rising smoothly 0.0003 → 0.0034, `actor/entropy` 0.412 → 0.386
  (no entropy collapse, no explosion), `training/off_policy/*` staleness 0 (sync trainer), no NaN/Inf anywhere in
  the log, `pg_loss` within −0.015 … 0.057.
* **Engine-mismatch diagnostics**: `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean` 0.0106–0.0132, `rollout_corr/kl`
  0.0052–0.0087, `rollout_corr/pearson` 0.991–0.994, `log_ppl_diff` +0.008 … +0.013 — all **flat from step 1**,
  with no trend over training (see 1.4 for why this is not a defect).
* **Runtime / memory** (`timing_s/*`, `perf/*`): gen 79–89 s, old_log_prob 6–11 s, ref 3–6 s, adv 0.2 s,
  update_actor 15–33 s, update_weights 3.5–6.5 s, validation 162–178 s, step 109–140 s; GPU memory 58–60 GB
  allocated / 69–70 GB reserved, stable across steps; no OOM, retries, restarts, or hangs in `train.log`
  (1601 lines, only the standard upstream warnings).
* **Batch balancing**: `global_seqlen/min` 8–11 k vs `max` 144–169 k before balancing and
  `balanced_min ≈ balanced_max` after, i.e. the Karmarkar–Karp balancing works and no rank is starved/overloaded.

### 1.4 Unusual observations examined and ruled out as causes

| observation | why it is not a defect / not causal |
|---|---|
| `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean` ≈ 0.011–0.013, above the FAQ's 0.01 "precision issue" line (`verl/docs/faq/faq.rst:170-212`) | It is constant from step 1 (before any update) and shows no drift with training; `rollout_corr/kl` ≈ 0.006 exceeds the entire 20-step policy drift (`kl_loss` 0.0034), and pearson ≥ 0.99. This is the bf16 vLLM-vs-FSDP numerical gap on a VL model with 2–3 k-token outputs. Its effect is bounded by PPO clipping (`pg_clipfrac` ≤ 7e-4) and it has no held-out signature. Weight sync is verified correct: `load_format=dummy` + `update_weights` at `on_init_end` gives a sane step-0 held-out accuracy (57 %), and `rollout_probs_diff_max` ≈ 1.0 is the usual single-token tail, not a desynced layer (a missing/stale parameter would produce a mismatch orders of magnitude larger and a garbage step-0 eval). |
| Training-side sampling overrides the model card (`temperature 1.0, top_k −1, top_p 1` vs card `0.7/20/0.8`) | This is the verl default rollout configuration (`RolloutConfig` block in `train.log`); exploration at T=1 is standard for GRPO, and the entropy/kl/clip series show it is stable. Validation correctly uses `val_kwargs` greedy n=1 (`agent_loop_tq.py:61-76`, `trainer_base.py:981`). |
| Format reward (0.1) never earned | Prompt template and grader are the upstream geo3k recipe; the Instruct model does not emit `<think>`; reward is therefore the pure accuracy term scaled by 0.9. Both train and held-out scores are interpretable and self-consistent. |
| Mini-batches are roughly length-ordered (v1 `ReplayBuffer._materialize_batch` iterates in completion order; `actor.shuffle=False`; `_balance_batch` sorts indices inside partitions) | Upstream v1 behaviour, not a staged modification. With token-mean aggregation and DP-all-reduced `batch_num_tokens`, each of the two optimizer updates per step is normalised over its own mini-batch; this introduces at most a mild length bias and no instability is visible (grad_norm, ppo_kl, entropy all flat). |
| Token-weighted advantage mean slightly negative (−0.12 … +0.02) | Wrong answers are longer than right ones, so token-mean weighting tilts negative; GRPO advantages are still zero-mean per prompt group. Expected. |
| 5–16 % truncation at 8192 tokens | Decreasing over training; budget identical to the upstream example; not a defect. |
| `param_offload=True`, `optimizer_offload=True`, gradient checkpointing, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.4` | Throughput-only settings; the run fits and timings are stable. |

### 1.5 Integrity / code checks performed (no discrepancies)

* `data/asset_manifest.json`: every listed file (train/test parquet, parity PNGs and `cases.json`, all model
  config/tokenizer/processor files and all four safetensors shards) matches the recorded sha256 and byte size.
* Train (2101) / test (601) parquet rows, prompts, answers and images match the source dataset; images are
  pixel-identical to the source; both the dataset path (`rl_dataset.py`) and the agent-loop path use
  `qwen_vl_utils.process_vision_info(image_patch_size=16)` consistently (`data.image_patch_size=16`).
* Qwen3-VL training-side forward (`verl/models/transformers/qwen3_vl.py`, `monkey_patch.py:416-453`) diffed
  against `transformers` 4.57.6: `fast_pos_embed_interpolate`, `_get_input_embeds` (masked_scatter + deepstack
  `visual_pos_masks`/`deepstack_visual_embeds`), and the 4-row M-RoPE position-id handling are identical (only
  a `grid_thw.device` fix differs). Position ids come from HF `Qwen3VLModel.get_rope_index` bound to the processor
  (`tokenizer.py:205-235`, `agent_loop.py:914-959`); the FSDP engine's remove-padding input preparation
  (`transformer_impl.py:1117-1301`, `extract_multi_modal_inputs`, `padding.py`) preserves per-sample order.
* Trainer loop (`trainer_base.py:443-503`, `trainer_sync.py`): weights are pushed to vLLM in `on_step_end`
  **before** `_validate`, so every held-out evaluation uses the freshly updated policy; validation runs greedy,
  n=1, over the full test split with `val_before_train=True` and `test_freq=5`.
* Loss / advantage / KL code (`core_algos.py`, `workers/utils/losses.py`): CPU unit tests
  (`tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py`, loss aggregation, dynamic policy losses, padding, metric utils)
  — 74 passed. (Remaining local collection errors are environment-only: the local CPU env has vllm 0.17.0 and no
  `transfer_queue`, whereas the recorded run executed from its own venv.)
* The effective config printed in `train.log` matches `run_qwen3vl_geo3k_grpo.sh` exactly (GRPO, std-normalised
  advantages, `use_kl_in_reward=False`, `use_kl_loss=True` coef 0.01 low_var_kl, entropy_coeff 0, clip 0.2 /
  dual-clip 3.0, lr 1e-6 constant, grad-clip 1.0, `ppo_mini_batch_size=16` ⇒ 2 updates/step, `ppo_epochs=1`,
  `rollout.n=5`, `max_model_len=10240`, `rollout_correction` disabled, `val_kwargs` greedy n=1).

---

## 2. Changes

**None.** No file under `/workspace` (launch script, `verl/`, data, model) was modified, and no log or metric
file was copied, edited, or created. `run_qwen3vl_geo3k_grpo.sh` is left exactly as staged, so the rerun keeps
writing `train.log`, `rollouts/`, `validation/`, `checkpoints/` and the offline W&B files to
`$LOG_DIR = $AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, with the same model, datasets, held-out split, 8 GPUs,
20-step budget and 5-step evaluation interval.

Optional, **not applied** (none is justified by the observed behaviour, and each would change the experiment
rather than fix a defect): `+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.disable_cascade_attn=True` or a
rollout-correction IS/TIS mode to shrink the engine mismatch; `actor_rollout_ref.actor.shuffle=True` to remove the
length ordering of mini-batches; a larger step budget / batch size if a measurable held-out gain (rather than a
health check) is the goal.

---

## 3. Expected effect of the rerun

Because nothing was changed, the 20-step rerun is expected to reproduce the recorded behaviour (up to sampling
noise; the rollout seed is 42 but vLLM batching/async scheduling is not bit-deterministic):

* `val-core/hiyouga/geometry3k/acc/mean@1`: ≈ 0.51 at step 0, then ≈ 0.52–0.56 at steps 5/10/15/20 — flat to
  slightly up, never materially below the step-0 baseline (no degradation is expected and none should be
  interpreted from ±2-point movements).
* `critic/score/mean` (training reward): rises from ≈ 0.40–0.49 in the first steps to ≈ 0.55–0.65 by steps
  15–20 (direction: up).
* `response_length/mean`: drifts down from ≈ 3 k toward ≈ 2.2–2.5 k tokens; `response_length/clip_ratio`:
  down from ≈ 0.11 to ≈ 0.05–0.08.
* `actor/kl_loss`: increases monotonically to ≈ 0.003–0.004; `actor/entropy` ≈ 0.39–0.41; `actor/grad_norm`
  < 1.0; `actor/pg_clipfrac` ≈ 0; `actor/ppo_kl` ≈ 0.
* `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean` ≈ 0.011–0.013 and `rollout_corr/pearson` ≈ 0.99, constant from step 1.
* Timing/memory within the recorded envelope (≈ 110–140 s per step, ≈ 170 s per validation, ≈ 60 GB allocated
  per GPU), run completing all 20 steps with five validations (steps 0, 5, 10, 15, 20) and one checkpoint at
  step 20.

The review is complete and the report is written at `/workspace/report.md` (12.7 KB). Nothing else in the workspace was touched (launch script and `verl/` still carry their original Oct 22 timestamps), and no training was launched.

## Summary

**Verdict: healthy — no defect found, no changes made.**

**Held-out evidence (primary):** greedy n=1 accuracy on the full 601-sample test split went 57.1 % → 61.2 % → 58.2 % → 58.7 % → 59.1 % at steps 0/5/10/15/20 — every post-training eval at or above baseline, all movements within the ≈2-point standard error. A paired analysis on the 194 samples with unique ground truths shows 14 wrong→right vs 18 right→wrong over steps 0→20 (sign test p≈0.6), i.e. flat within noise, no degradation.

**Training-side evidence:** sampled reward rose 0.456 → 0.590 (sharpening + fewer truncations), response length 3067 → ≈2290 tokens, truncation 11 % → 5–8 %, kl_loss 0.0003 → 0.0034 smooth, entropy 0.41 → 0.39, grad_norm 0.29–0.73, pg_clipfrac ≤7e-4, ppo_kl ≈ 0, stable timings and memory, no NaN/OOM/restarts.

**Unusual-but-non-causal items** (each connected to observed behaviour in the report): engine mismatch `rollout_probs_diff_mean` ≈0.011–0.013 is constant from step 1 with pearson ≥0.99 and no held-out signature; T=1.0 full-vocab sampling is the verl default (validation correctly greedy, verified in `agent_loop_tq.py`); format bonus never earned because the Instruct model skips `<think>` (grader identical to upstream); length-ordered mini-batches are upstream v1 behaviour with no visible instability.

**Integrity checks:** all assets match the manifest sha256s; Qwen3-VL monkey patches, deepstack/M-RoPE position-id path and FSDP input prep diffed clean against transformers 4.57.6; validation uses freshly synced weights (`on_step_end` → `update_weights` before `_validate`); 74 CPU unit tests on the loss/advantage code passed; effective config in `train.log` matches the script.

**Expected rerun:** same trajectory — training reward up, held-out ≈0.51–0.56 and never materially below step 0, truncation down, KL rising to ≈0.003–0.004, logs still written to `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`.
